section_summary.extract_value: This section details the examination of the factorial validity of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) using a sample of 2393 participants. It tests one-dimensional and two-dimensional models, ultimately finding that a two-dimensional model, after the removal of four items, provided the best fit and was invariant across sex. The section also reports gender differences in General Body Appreciation scores and correlations between General Body Appreciation and BMI for women (r = -0.32) and men (r = -0.02).

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the examination of factorial validity for a one-dimensional and several two-dimensional models of body appreciation, ultimately identifying a best-fitting two-factor model after item deletions. It reports on the invariance of this model across sex, mean differences in General Body Appreciation between men and women, and correlations between General Body Appreciation and BMI for both sexes. The study involved a total sample of N=2393 participants, with specific sample sizes for men (n=1074) and women (n=1319) presented in Table 1.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the results of confirmatory factor analyses (CFA) for different models of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) using a sample of N = 2393. It describes testing one-dimensional and two-dimensional models, ultimately finding the best fit for a two-dimensional model after removing four items. The section also reports on the invariance of the model across sex and discusses correlations between General Body Appreciation and BMI for men and women.
